ground_truth.description: `_checkpoint` creates a new epoch with the same timestamp for `increase_amount`, ignoring the new lock in `balanceOfNFT`, reducing voting power.
ground_truth.root_cause: `_checkpoint` creates a new epoch with the same timestamp for `increase_amount`, ignoring the new lock in `balanceOfNFT`, reducing voting power.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: A test locks 500e18, increases by 500e18 in one tx, and shows reduced bribe rewards compared to separate locks.
ground_truth.fix_description: In `_checkpoint`, overwrite the latest point if timestamps match, else append a new one. Status: Mitigation confirmed.

vulnerabilities.explanation: _checkpoint appends a new point_history entry even when timestamps match (same block/tx). When create_lock followed by increase_amount executes in one transaction, the second call creates a duplicate-timestamp epoch. balanceOfNFT reads the latest point but ignores the updated lock amount for that timestamp, under-calculating voting power.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. User calls create_lock(500e18, ...) then increase_amount(tokenId, 500e18) in same tx. 2. First _checkpoint records epoch N at t=block.timestamp. 3. Second _checkpoint appends epoch N+1 at identical t with only the incremental amount. 4. balanceOfNFT and downstream bribe calculations use the stale point, granting permanently lower voting power and reduced rewards.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: In _checkpoint, before appending, check if point_history[_epoch].ts == block.timestamp; if so, overwrite the latest point instead of incrementing epoch.

prediction.overall_explanation: The documented checkpoint logic error exists in the supplied code and produces a concrete, user-triggerable reduction in voting power when multiple lock operations occur in one transaction.
